key_insight: Translation-method bounds sharpen the known conductivity–shear-modulus trade-off for 3D isotropic two-phase composites, while optimized microstructures remain slightly below the bounds.
engineering_relevance: These bounds provide benchmarks for designing composites that combine electrical or thermal conduction with resistance to shear deformation.
method: Compute conductivity–shear-modulus cross-property bounds using the translation method.
Run unit-cell topology optimization from thousands of distinct initial structures.
Compare designs with isotropic bounds using an effective-medium model of randomly oriented grains.
evidence_signal: Across thousands of initial structures, the best jointly performing designs were consistently bicontinuous and triply periodic minimal surface-like, with a small remaining gap to the bounds.
watch_item: Attainability remains unresolved, and comparisons rely on an effective-medium approximation of macroscopic isotropy.
paper_title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
